forces.mechanism: Dealers delta-hedge the options they are short or long. When dealers are long gamma around a strike, they sell rallies and buy dips — suppressing volatility and pinning price toward the strike into expiry. When short gamma, they must buy rallies and sell dips — amplifying moves through the strike. Public data shows where gamma is concentrated, not the dealers’ sign; the conventional assumption (customers net long calls above spot, long puts below) is unverified.

forces.invalidation: Skew flipping sign; a large expiry rolling off removes the pinning effect.

forces.mechanism: Depth is the market’s shock absorber. Price impact of a flow ≈ flow ÷ available liquidity, so the same ETF redemption or liquidation moves price far more in a thin book. Displayed depth also withdraws during volatility (market makers widen or pull quotes), so realised liquidity in a sell-off is lower than the snapshot suggests — which is how thin markets turn ordinary selling into cascades.
forces.interpretation: Liquidity is broadly stable versus last week.  Displayed ≠ executed liquidity: treat impact estimates as a best case.
forces.invalidation: ±1% depth falling more than 15% within a week, especially during a price decline.
forces.watch: Depth during US hours and around macro releases; bid-side depth on Coinbase (ETF execution venue); whether depth falls as price falls (withdrawal) or holds (absorption).

forces.mechanism: Funding is the price longs pay shorts to keep perpetuals anchored to spot. High positive funding means demand for leveraged long exposure exceeds supply — crowded positioning that bleeds carry and is vulnerable to a flush. Negative funding means shorts are crowded and a rally forces them to buy. Basis on dated futures shows the same thing for institutional (cash-and-carry) demand; a falling basis can force basis-trade unwinds (ETF selling + futures buying).
forces.interpretation: Funding is in a normal carry range; positioning is not crowded on either side.
forces.watch: Funding resets at 00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC; venue dispersion (a single venue spiking often precedes local liquidations); basis falling toward T-bill yield (basis-trade unwind risk).

# BTC Market Intelligence — 2026-10-03

**$84,828 · −1.1% 24h · +1.1% 7d · +7.7% 30d**  
**Regime:** Macro-led — BTC is moving with equities, the dollar and real yields.  
_Data through 2026-10-03 14:56 UTC · 4 sources unavailable (3 region-blocked from US servers, 1 inactive)_
**On-chain cycle:** Optimism · Neutral / mid-cycle · momentum constructive  

**What changed (≥1.5σ):** BTC–Nasdaq 30d corr 0.20 → 0.58 (6.7σ, 24h); Stablecoin supply $307.80B → $311.89B (2.3σ, 7d); Funding (ann.) 6.2% → 0.2% (-2.1σ, 24h); 10y real yield 2.93% → 2.88% (-1.7σ, 24h).
